request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: Logistic run 1 (PR-AUC 0.6809, SD 0.0595) trails the best LightGBM run 7 (0.7355) by 0.0546, which is slightly below one fold SD (~0.06), so by the simplicity rule the simple model is preferred. Run 5, logistic with agent features, scores 0.6895, so it is a slightly better logistic option, and its gain over run 1 is well within noise.
Fold SDs of 0.056-0.079 are large relative to the gaps between configs. Run 7 beats run 2 (0.7047) by 0.03 and run 3 (0.7328) by only 0.003, so the top configs cannot be told apart statistically.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin, so it is suspicion rather than confirmed fraud. Models may be learning the labeling process, for example claim volume or rule-based flags, rather than real fraud.

ROC-AUC of about 0.94 across all models, including a plain logistic regression, is high for fraud detection and may indicate that the label is largely determined by simple size or volume features. This is suspiciously good and worth checking for leakage.

Precision@50 (0.74-0.78) is only a proxy for the ~100-provider audit queue, and k=100 was not measured. The 'agent' features were not examined for leakage or for dependence on the time window, and the claims span only about 13 months.
Seven configs were tried on the same folds, so the best-of-N PR-AUC is optimistically biased. Class weighting and SMOTE gave no clear benefit, and SMOTE was never tried.
Run 1 and run 5 are close in score. I picked run 1 as the simplest option, but run 5 is a defensible alternative.
